Priya (Support): Hey team, escalation from AcmeRetail — they see a sudden spike of 429s + elevated p95 latency after a canary this morning. They say it started right when traffic shifted regions (us-west-2 -> eu-central-1). Customer hit us via the hosted API. Can we triage? :eyes:

Jonas (SRE): Thanks. Do we have their org id and example request/response headers? Useful: X-RateLimit-* headers or X-Redwood-Routing decision. High-level: cross-region fallbacks consume the target region's burst/quota when routed; if source is saturated and fails over we'll see cross_region_retries + possible 429s if target also nearing limits.

Marta (Runtime Eng): Noted — there's also a runtime kernel tweak we rolled into us-west-2 last night (smaller-threads optimization). It reduced p99 latency for small sequences but lowered sustained tokens/sec on some model variants. Could make capacity lower than expected under long sequences.

Priya (Support): Customer pasted a snippet, here's the response headers they forwarded: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 11 Oct 2025 15:12:03 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1697049125
X-Redwood-Route: us-west-2 (fallback -> eu-central-1)
X-Redwood-Fallback-Count: 3
Content-Type: application/json
```
Body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"region capacity exhausted"}`

Jonas (SRE): That X-Redwood-Route header is exactly what I wanted to see (fallback -> eu-central-1). Looks like us-west-2 dropped requests and we retried to eu-central-1 which then exhausted remaining burst. Can you confirm whether AcmeRetail is on a reserved Dedicated pool or hosted metered?

Eve (Customer): We're hosted (no dedicated). We started a canary and ramped quickly from 10rps to 350rps over 3 minutes. We assumed fallback would autoscale. Sorry if we triggered this.

Jonas (SRE): Ok hosted — autoscaling has limits and regional burst credits are finite. Quick repro steps for us:
1) From a loadbox in us-west-2 run `wrk -c 200 -t 8 -d 120 --timeout 10s \"-H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\"`
2) Watch `X-RateLimit-Remaining` in responses and `routing.failover_count` in metrics.

Marta (Runtime Eng): Also check metrics: 
- Query: `sum(rate(redwood_serving_tokens_total{region=~"us-west-2|eu-central-1"}[1m])) by (region)`
- Look at `routing.cross_region_retries` and `quota.burst.tokens_used{org="acmeretail"}`
If the kernel tweak is the cause, tokens/sec in us-west-2 will be lower than expected and failovers will spike.

Priya (Support): Customer also attached a minimal repro curl they ran: ```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2' -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"model":"gpt-open-3b"}'
```
They said removing the region header dropped them to eu-central-1 and they still saw intermittent 429s.

Jonas (SRE): Two immediate mitigation options for hosted customers: 1) set regional affinity / prefer_region to pin traffic to a healthy region if they have capacity elsewhere: `X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: us-east-1` (short-term), or 2) request a temporary increase in burst credits / reserve additional capacity for the org. I'll check current cross-region capacity and burst pool.

Chris (Account): If they want a short-term bump I'm happy to coordinate quota increases — need org id and expected rps profile and which models. Priya, can you capture that?

Priya (Support): Sent request to customer for org_id + model + 95th token length distribution. Also asked if they can run the wrk blister test above from us-west-2 and from eu-central-1 (so we can compare).

Marta (Runtime Eng): If you want a guarded rollback of the kernel tweak in us-west-2 I can do a canary rollback. My ask: let us confirm the metrics first — if tokens/sec drop lines up with their traffic time window I'll rollback. If rollback, expect ~10-15m to propagate.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout job `runtime-kernel-tweak` started in us-west-2 at 2025-10-11T02:45:10Z by marta (job-id: rdw-deploy-7782).

Eve (Customer): We can provide org id: acme-retail-42. Model is gpt-open-3b, typical request tokens ~512, burst to ~400rps at peak. Need this resolved — production is impacted.

Jonas (SRE): Thanks. Actions:
- Priya: attach logs + their wrk output to TKT-5621 and request timeframe for the canary start.
- Marta: confirm kernel metrics in us-west-2; rollback if metrics align.
- Chris: liaise on temporary burst increase for acme-retail-42.
- I'll enable a short routing policy to prefer eu-central-1 for new requests from the org while we stabilize (non-destructive).

Marta (Runtime Eng): I'm pulling `redwood_serving_tokens_total{region="us-west-2",model="gpt-open-3b"}` now and comparing to historical 95th. If I see the decline I'll prepare rollback and ping here before executing.

Priya (Support): All noted. I've opened TKT-5621 and added the headers snippet + their timeline. Adding wrk repro steps too.

Jonas (SRE): Follow-ups to monitor post-mitigation: `routing.cross_region_retries`, `quota.burst.tokens_used{org="acme-retail-42"}`, `redwood_serving_latency_p95{region=~"us-west-2|eu-central-1"}`. I'll keep an eye on alerting.

Chris (Account): I'll draft a one-time burst credit increase while Eng confirms rollback status. Priya — please forward expected peak rps and token sizes.

Eve (Customer): Appreciate it. We'll throttle our ramp for now to 60rps and share load tests.

Priya (Support): Great. Closing the immediate loop — will update TKT-5621 when Marta confirms metrics or rollback. :white_check_mark:
